name: FRTX
description: RTX-style post processing for Geometry Dash: emissive bloom, volumetric light rays, lens flare, halation and cinematic grading, with a live in-game tuner.

tuner-info.name: Tune it in game
tuner-info.description: Press F8 while playing a level to open an overlay with every setting below, and adjust them while the game runs. Arrow keys move and adjust, Shift is coarse, Alt is fine, R resets a value, 1-4 apply a preset, Escape closes.

presets.name: Apply a preset
presets.description: Writes that preset's values into the settings below. Everything stays editable afterwards -- a preset is a starting point, not a lock.

ray-presets.name: Light Ray Styles
ray-presets.description: Presets built around the light ray pass. Dawn is a low warm sun with long shafts, Cathedral drops hard shafts from overhead, Eclipse is a dark frame around a tight corona, Aurora is cool and hazy, and Inferno is a hot close sun with heavy halation.

style-presets.name: Styles
style-presets.description: Different looks rather than different intensities. Neon suits glow-heavy levels, Cinematic goes for filmic warmth, Dreamy for a soft wide haze, Noir for monochrome contrast, Vivid for punch with little glow, and Sunbeam turns on light rays.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Master switch. When off the game renders completely untouched and no GPU memory is used.

enable-in-editor.name: In Editor
enable-in-editor.description: Also apply the effect inside the level editor.

exclude-ui.name: Exclude UI
exclude-ui.description: Draw the gameplay UI on top of the effect instead of through it, so the attempt counter and progress bar stay crisp.

debug-view.name: Debug View
debug-view.description: 0 = normal, 1 = captured scene, 2 = bloom, 3 = streaks, 4 = light rays, 5 = flare and halation. Invaluable for setting the bloom threshold.

bloom-enabled.name: Bloom
bloom-enabled.description: Makes bright objects, glow and particles bleed light into their surroundings.

bloom-intensity.name: Intensity
bloom-intensity.description: How strongly the blurred highlights are added back on top of the scene.

bloom-threshold.name: Threshold
bloom-threshold.description: Brightness a pixel must reach before it starts to glow. Lower values make more of the screen bloom.

bloom-knee.name: Soft Knee
bloom-knee.description: Softness of the threshold. 0 is a hard cutoff, higher values fade highlights in gradually.

bloom-emissive-bias.name: Emissive Bias
bloom-emissive-bias.description: Biases the glow towards saturated colours, so neon and glow objects bloom hard while bright backgrounds stay put. Pure white still glows.

bloom-bg-suppress.name: Background Suppression
bloom-bg-suppress.description: Reduces glow in areas whose surroundings are already bright, so a lone bright object keeps its halo while a big washed-out background loses most of it. Raise this when a bright sky is blooming as hard as the objects in front of it.

bloom-bg-radius.name: Background Scale
bloom-bg-radius.description: How wide a neighbourhood counts as 'the background', as a fraction of screen height. Large values only suppress screen-scale washes; small values also dim the middle of big glowing objects.

bloom-radius.name: Radius
bloom-radius.description: Scales the blur step size. Larger values spread the glow further at the cost of some fidelity.

bloom-spread.name: Spread
bloom-spread.description: How large the halo reads. Low values keep the glow tight against the object; high values let the widest blur levels through.

bloom-levels.name: Levels
bloom-levels.description: Number of blur levels. 1 is a tight glow and cheapest, 3 gives a wide cinematic falloff.

bloom-scale.name: Resolution Scale
bloom-scale.description: Resolution of the bloom buffers relative to the screen. Lower is faster and slightly softer.

bloom-tint.name: Tint
bloom-tint.description: Colours the glow. White leaves it the colour of whatever is glowing.

streak-intensity.name: Intensity
streak-intensity.description: Horizontal light streaks off bright points, like a cinema lens. Off by default: showcase levels glow radially rather than streaking. Needs bloom enabled.

streak-length.name: Length
streak-length.description: How far the streaks reach across the screen.

streak-tint.name: Tint
streak-tint.description: A faint cool tint is what reads as an anamorphic lens rather than as more bloom.

rays-intensity.name: Intensity
rays-intensity.description: Volumetric-looking shafts of light radiating from a point. Needs bloom enabled. 0 disables the pass entirely.

rays-density.name: Density
rays-density.description: How far along the ray direction the samples are spread. Higher values give longer shafts.

rays-decay.name: Decay
rays-decay.description: How quickly a ray fades as it travels. Just below 1 gives long soft shafts; lower values cut them short.

rays-weight.name: Weight
rays-weight.description: Contribution of each sample along the ray.

rays-samples.name: Samples
rays-samples.description: Samples per pixel. The single biggest cost in this pass; lower it first if rays are slow.

rays-jitter.name: Jitter
rays-jitter.description: Randomises where along the ray each pixel starts sampling. Without it every pixel samples at the same distances and the shafts show concentric stepping; with it that banding becomes fine noise instead. Costs nothing.

rays-occlusion.name: Occlusion
rays-occlusion.description: Dims rays where the scene in front of them is dark, so shafts pass behind solid objects instead of over them. This is most of what makes them read as light in the air rather than as an overlay.

rays-shimmer.name: Shimmer
rays-shimmer.description: Slowly varies ray strength with angle, like light moving through disturbed air. Subtle values only.

rays-sun.name: Sun Disc
rays-sun.description: Draws a glowing disc at the ray origin, so the shafts have a visible source. 0 leaves the origin invisible.

rays-sun-size.name: Sun Size
rays-sun-size.description: Radius of that disc, as a fraction of screen height.

rays-origin-mode.name: Origin
rays-origin-mode.description: 0 = a fixed point on screen, 1 = follow the player.

rays-origin-x.name: Origin X
rays-origin-x.description: Horizontal position of the light source. 0 is the left edge and 1 the right; values outside that put the sun off screen, which shafts still reach in from.

rays-origin-y.name: Origin Y
rays-origin-y.description: Vertical position of the light source. 0 is the bottom edge and 1 the top; values outside that put the sun off screen.

rays-tint.name: Tint
rays-tint.description: Colours the shafts. A warm tint reads as sunlight.

flare-intensity.name: Ghosts
flare-intensity.description: Ghost images of bright areas mirrored through the centre of the screen, the way light bounces between lens elements. Needs bloom enabled. 0 disables the pass.

flare-spacing.name: Ghost Spacing
flare-spacing.description: How far apart the ghosts sit along the line through the screen centre.

halation.name: Halation
halation.description: A warm red bleed around highlights, the way film stock scatters light back through its own base. Very different from bloom: it is wide, soft and strongly coloured.

lens-distortion.name: Distortion
lens-distortion.description: Barrel distortion at positive values, pincushion at negative. Small amounts read as a real lens; large ones as a fisheye.

clarity.name: Amount
clarity.description: Local contrast. Lifts edge and material detail so the frame reads as though it has depth. Pushed hard it rings bright outlines.

clarity-radius.name: Radius
clarity-radius.description: Radius in pixels. Small values sharpen, larger values give broad depth instead.

clarity-taps.name: Taps
clarity-taps.description: Samples used to estimate the blur clarity works against. 4 is half the cost and near indistinguishable at small radii; 8 is smoother at large ones. This is the most expensive part of the final pass.

tonemap-enabled.name: Filmic Tonemapping
tonemap-enabled.description: Applies an ACES filmic curve so bright areas roll off smoothly instead of clipping to white.

exposure.name: Exposure
exposure.description: Overall brightness multiplier applied before tonemapping.

black-point.name: Black Point
black-point.description: Crushes the darkest values to true black. A little of this is most of what separates graded footage from a filter.

split-shadow.name: Shadow Tone
split-shadow.description: Tints the shadows only. Positive values cool them towards blue, the classic cinematic split.

split-highlight.name: Highlight Tone
split-highlight.description: Tints the highlights only. Positive values warm them towards orange.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Whole-image white balance. Negative cools towards blue, positive warms towards orange.

tint.name: Tint
tint.description: Negative values push towards magenta, positive towards green.

vignette.name: Vignette
vignette.description: Darkens the corners of the screen. 0 disables it.

vignette-roundness.name: Vignette Roundness
vignette-roundness.description: 0 follows the shape of the screen, 1 is a perfect circle.

vignette-softness.name: Vignette Softness
vignette-softness.description: How gradually the darkening comes in from the corners.

chromatic.name: Chromatic Aberration
chromatic.description: Splits red and blue towards the edges of the screen, like a real lens. 0 disables it.

grain.name: Film Grain
grain.description: Adds animated noise. Keep this very low; 0 disables it.

dither.name: Dithering
dither.description: Adds an imperceptible amount of noise to hide colour banding in smooth gradients.
